paper_title: Revisiting Graph Modification via Disk Scaling: From One Radius to Interval-Based Radii
classifications: Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: Fomin et al. [17] also studied an optimization variant where we scale (at most) k disks P and minimize p∈S |1 − r(p)|. Generalizing our algorithmic results to this min-variant is non-trivial and remains open. In particular, we cannot simply adapt the optimization function of the LP due to our (maximized) “slack-variable” ε (and only determining the disks to scale is not sufficient since disks might require different radii). It is also open whether Scaling To Cluster admits a polynomial kernel for k or is in NP. Finally, it would be interesting to combine scaling with other modification operations, such as disk dispersion [16].
